name: Login routes
purpose: Owns the HTTP surface of the sign-in flow: the GET /login form page, the POST /login submission handler, the GET /login/verify consume handler, and the POST /logout handler. The routes compose the magic-link manager, the session manager, the email delivery adapter, and the principal registry into one HTTP-shaped orchestration; anti-enumeration timing and per-route rate-limit configuration live here.
responsibilities: Serve GET /login as a page with exactly one email input and no password input (AC-3101-1).
Accept POST /login with an application/x-www-form-urlencoded email field and return a 200 with a generic body (AC-3101-2, AC-3106-1, AC-3106-2).
Enforce an anti-enumeration budget on POST /login so no response returns earlier than the configured wall-clock floor and no branch's outcome affects the observable timing (AC-3106-3).

Configure per-route rate limits on POST /login (default five per minute per client key) and on GET /login/verify (default twenty per minute per client key), emitting 429 with Retry-After on breach (AC-3107-1, AC-3107-2, AC-3107-4).
On registered submissions, call the magic-link manager to mint a token, compose the sign-in URL from the deployment base URL, and hand the URL to the email delivery adapter (AC-3101-3).

On GET /login/verify with a valid unconsumed unexpired token, call the session manager to issue a session, set the session cookie with Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite=Lax, and redirect to the configured post-sign-in route (AC-3101-4, AC-3104-1, AC-3104-2, AC-3104-3).
On GET /login/verify with any other token value, return a 401 with a generic sign-in-failed body and no Set-Cookie (AC-3101-5).
On POST /logout, call the session manager to invalidate the presented handle and return a Set-Cookie that clears the session cookie (AC-3105-1, AC-3105-2).
internalStructure: One routes module registered onto the project's HTTP framework instance; the module receives its collaborators (magic-link manager, session manager, adapter, registry) as constructor arguments. The anti-enumeration budget is an injected constant with a default of 800 ms; per-route rate limits are configured on the framework's rate-limit plugin, not implemented in the module.

interfaces.name: app
interfaces.description: The project's HTTP framework instance the routes are registered onto; the framework must expose a per-route rate-limit configuration surface.

interfaces.name: magicLinks
interfaces.description: TAC-501 instance; the routes call mint and consume through it.

interfaces.name: sessions
interfaces.description: TAC-502 instance; the routes call issueSession, invalidateSession, and cookie helpers through it.

interfaces.name: adapter
interfaces.description: TAC-504 instance; the routes call adapter.send through it.

interfaces.name: registry
interfaces.description: TAC-505 instance; the routes call registry.isRegistered through it and consume only the boolean result.

dependencies.name: Session manager
dependencies.description: Provides session issue, invalidate, and cookie shape.

dependencies.name: Email delivery adapter
dependencies.description: Provides the send method the routes call.

tradeoffs: Rate-limit ceilings and the anti-enumeration budget are conservative defaults that make operator retry cheap and abuse expensive; a project with a heavier legitimate load overrides the ceilings and states the trade in its own ADR. The routes are the only auth-shaped HTTP surface the blueprint ships; projects wanting a bearer-token flow instead layer a project-authored ADR superseding auth-model and provide their own routes.
